definitions.problem: Giving a 'capture' task to a squad that was already removed crashes: task_objects.script: attempt to index field '?' (a nil value). Also: a story task whose target NPC is not on his job (Wild Napr while the Flea Market is fighting, or after he died offline) aborts the game: wrong target for storyline quest: logic@work5,gar_smart_terrain_6_3. 'Capture' tasks: when the camp is taken, the script announces the counter-attack through the first allied squad in the camp. If no squad is there any more, or the former owner is unknown, it indexes a missing value and the game stops; and it waits for the announcement to end without a time limit, so the task can hang for ever. 'Defend' tasks: the time of the last call for help is set only when a defending squad is in the camp; without one the next check compares with a missing time and the game stops.
definitions.description: The capture task is given only if the squad still exists; a story task whose target NPC is missing is simply not given for now. The counter-attack is skipped when there is nobody to announce it, the wait for the announcement ends after a minute, and the 'defend' call time is always set (also when an older save is loaded without it). The delayed 'defend' task also tolerates an attacking squad that has vanished or is between camps. A counter-attack no longer takes a neighbouring squad that has its own scripted target elsewhere.

definitions.problem: Every time a mechanic is asked which "find the tool" tasks he can give, the script first builds a new task and takes a new id from the task id pool, and only then notices that this task already exists. On load the mechanic is restored from the table the tasks are stored under; nothing new is written into the save.

definitions.problem: Every NPC in a camp must hold one of the camp's jobs. When more NPCs arrive than there are suitable free jobs (two squads meet in the small wagon camp of the Dark Valley, for example), the game stops with 'Insufficient smart_terrain jobs <camp>'.
definitions.description: An NPC that finds no free job does a suitable job that is already held, alongside its owner. The job stays its owner's: when the extra NPC leaves, dies or moves on, the owner's place and the camp's record of who does which job are not touched, and the extra NPC takes a free job as soon as there is one. The game still stops if the camp has no job at all that suits the NPC. SRP avoids the situation by reworking squad movement; this is our own smaller remedy. Its bookkeeping was run outside the game (register, leave, death, job swap, periodic re-selection); it has not been run in the game.
